security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown, Cloudflare API examples, SQL exec calls, and documented placeholder secrets. Confirmed risks remain in Sandbox examples that promote unsafe shell execution, token-in-URL cloning, and untrusted command construction, plus Tunnel service-install examples that require administrator approval.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell pattern with a pinned, checksum-verified install flow or documented package manager steps.

remediation.issue: Sandbox examples interpolate request-controlled values into shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Use allowlists, strict URL validation, argument arrays where available, and avoid shell interpolation for repo, branch, and code values.

remediation.issue: A git clone example embeds GITHUB_TOKEN in a URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use credential helpers, short-lived scoped tokens, or environment-based authentication that does not expose tokens in command strings.

remediation.issue: Tunnel examples install and enable persistent system services.
remediation.suggestion: Mark these commands as manual administrator actions and include rollback, audit, and least-privilege guidance.

content.user_title: Build Cloudflare Apps With Current Guidance
content.value_statement: Cloudflare projects span many products, and outdated details can cause broken deployments. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to focused Cloudflare references and current source checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects the right Cloudflare product reference for Workers, Pages, storage, AI, networking, security, and infrastructure-as-code tasks.
Guides Workers, Pages, Durable Objects, Workflows, Containers, Cron Triggers, and Tail Workers implementation choices.
Covers Cloudflare storage patterns for KV, D1, R2, Queues, Hyperdrive, Vectorize, and Secrets Store.
Includes references for Wrangler, Miniflare, Terraform, Pulumi, GraphQL Analytics, and REST API workflows.
Highlights when to retrieve current Cloudflare docs, changelogs, Workers types, and Wrangler schema.
Documents security, networking, media, real-time, email, analytics, and AI platform features.
limitations: The reference files may be stale; verify limits, pricing, API signatures, and compatibility dates against current Cloudflare docs.
It does not provide credentials, account access, or permission grants for Cloudflare resources.
Some examples require careful review before production use, especially sandbox command execution and service installation.
It cannot guarantee that third-party SDK versions or platform behavior remain unchanged.

use_cases.title: Plan a Workers Project
use_cases.description: Choose Workers, Pages, Durable Objects, KV, D1, R2, and bindings for a new Cloudflare application.

use_cases.title: Operate Cloudflare Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Use Wrangler, Terraform, Pulumi, Tunnels, WAF, DDoS, and observability references for reliable operations.

use_cases.title: Design AI and Data Workflows
use_cases.description: Combine Workers AI, Vectorize, AI Gateway, R2, D1, Queues, and analytics patterns with current documentation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Cloudflare Product
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to build [goal]. Use this Cloudflare skill to recommend the right product, key tradeoffs, and docs to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Worker Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cloudflare architecture for [application]. Include Workers, storage, bindings, deployment steps, and current docs I should verify.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Deployment Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cloudflare deployment plan for gaps in security, limits, bindings, Wrangler configuration, and observability: [plan].

prompt_templates.title: Migrate With IaC Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from [current setup] to Cloudflare using Terraform or Pulumi. Include validation, rollback, secrets, and docs checks.

output_examples.input: Choose storage for user sessions, product images, and analytics events.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends KV or Durable Objects for sessions, R2 for images, and Analytics Engine or Queues for event workflows.

output_examples.input: Review a Wrangler deployment for a Pages Functions app.
output_examples.output: The response highlights binding checks, compatibility dates, environment variables, local testing, and current docs to verify before release.

output_examples.input: Plan a secure Cloudflare Tunnel rollout.
output_examples.output: The response covers tunnel credentials, least-privilege tokens, service installation review, ingress rules, logging, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Verify current docs before using limits, pricing, API schemas, or compatibility dates.
Use least-privilege Cloudflare tokens and keep secrets in approved secret managers.
Treat shell, sandbox, and service-install examples as privileged operations that require human review.
anti_patterns: Copying reference snippets into production without checking current docs or permissions.
Embedding API tokens in URLs, logs, commits, or shared prompts.
Exposing sandbox, tunnel, browser rendering, or email workflows without authentication and rate limits.

faq.question: Does this skill replace the official Cloudflare documentation?
faq.answer: No. It provides routing and reference context, but current Cloudflare docs remain the source of truth.

faq.question: Can it deploy resources in my Cloudflare account?
faq.answer: No. It can guide commands and configuration, but users must provide credentials and approve changes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What Cloudflare areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Workers, Pages, storage, AI, networking, security, media, analytics, and infrastructure-as-code references.

faq.question: Why should I verify details before using them?
faq.answer: Cloudflare limits, APIs, pricing, compatibility dates, and platform behavior can change after references are written.

faq.question: What should I review most carefully?
faq.answer: Review examples involving shell commands, sandbox execution, service installation, credentials, and public endpoints.
